home.tagline: A Vue 3 UI library with a real Vue Vapor build.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.intro: A Vue 3 component library with a full Vue Vapor build and an animation-agnostic design: plain CSS by default, or bring your own animation library.
gettingStarted.vaporIntro: Both builds ship from the same package and source. Pick whichever your app runs, or mix both (Vue 3.6 supports VDOM/Vapor interop). Every component page has the same toggle to compare them.
gettingStarted.installIntro: vael-ui is published on npm. Install it with whichever package manager you use:
gettingStarted.usageImportNote: Import the stylesheet once in your entry point (see {link} for base-style setup):
gettingStarted.usageIntro: Then use any component: from 'vael-ui' for the classic VDOM build, or 'vael-ui/vapor' for the compiled Vapor build (Vue 3.6's no-virtual-DOM mode). Same props either way:
gettingStarted.darkModeIntro: CSS-only: responds to <html data-theme="dark">, falling back to prefers-color-scheme. No toggle UI shipped; useColorScheme() handles persistence and OS-preference updates:
gettingStarted.directivesIntro: v-tooltip and v-scroll-mask aren't global by default. If you use either in more than one component, register them once:
gettingStarted.directivesNote: v-tooltip also needs a <TooltipHost /> mounted once. In a Vapor app, import both directives from vael-ui/vapor instead.

globalSetup.title: Global setup
globalSetup.intro: Three singletons. Mount each once, anywhere in your app, and every other component reaches it automatically.
globalSetup.tooltipHostIntro: Powers every v-tooltip. Without one mounted, tooltips silently never appear.
globalSetup.tooltipHostOptions: It takes the same options every individual tooltip can override:
globalSetup.dialogHostIntro: Renders whatever openDialog() creates imperatively. Not needed for a <Dialog v-model:open> in your own template. No props, no configuration.
globalSetup.toasterIntro: Renders whatever {code} creates. Has real configuration, so it keeps {link}.
globalSetup.allTogetherIntro: Mount all three once, wherever your app's root template lives:

tailwind.layerNote: vael-ui ships in {layer}. Tailwind's utility classes are unlayered, and unlayered CSS always wins over a layer regardless of specificity or import order, so a Tailwind utility on a vael-ui component always overrides the library's default. No {important}, no specificity fights, nothing to configure. See {link} for the general mechanics.
tailwind.mergingIntro: Every component accepts a ui prop for part classes (e.g. :ui="{'{'} root: 'my-class' {'}'}"). To resolve conflicting Tailwind utilities there the way tailwind-merge would (last one wins per property), wire it up once:
tailwind.mergingNote: Every ui.* part class in the tree now passes through twMerge.

stylingLayers.title: Styling and cascade layers
stylingLayers.intro: vael-ui ships in {layer}. Unlayered CSS always wins over a layer regardless of specificity, so a plain, unlayered base reset silently overrides vael-ui internals. Fix: put your base styles in a layer too, ordered first.
stylingLayers.orderNote: Two files, that's it. Import order here only controls layer position, nothing else, an unlayered override anywhere always still wins regardless of load order.
stylingLayers.overrideNote: Deliberately overriding one component ({code} prop, a Tailwind utility) wants your rule to win, keep that CSS unlayered as it already is by default. See {link}.

animation.title: Bring your own animation
animation.intro: Every component that animates ships a plain CSS transition, but exposes a real escape hatch to drive it with GSAP, motion-v, or nothing at all. Check a component's own Props/Slots/Exposed tables for which of these it has, not every component has all three.
animation.motionCssIntro: false disables the built-in CSS transition, the component still changes state instantly, leaving the DOM ready for you to animate.
animation.forceMountIntro: Keeps content mounted while closed instead of removing it on v-if. Pair with <AnimatePresence> and the default slot's isClosing flag to own exit timing yourself.
animation.beforeCloseIntro: For imperative libraries: pass a function that receives done. The component stays mounted and isClosing until you call it.

descriptions.ConfigProvider: Wraps your app to provide theming, i18n, and class-merging to every component below it.
descriptions.Button: A clickable action with variants, sizes, loading states, and icon slots built in.
descriptions.SplitButton: A primary action fused with a chevron that opens alternate actions in a dropdown.
descriptions.Toolbar: A horizontal strip for grouping related actions, with roving keyboard focus.
descriptions.SpeedDial: A floating action button that fans out into secondary actions on demand.
descriptions.Dial: A circular drag control for picking a numeric value, like a volume knob.
descriptions.SelectButton: A segmented control for choosing one (or several) values from a short list.
descriptions.Input: A single-line text field with sizes, states, and slots for icons or hints.
descriptions.Textarea: A multi-line text field that can auto-grow with its content.
descriptions.InputNumber: A numeric field with increment/decrement controls and format-aware parsing.
descriptions.OtpInput: A row of single-character boxes for one-time codes, with paste and auto-advance.
descriptions.Checkbox: A tri-state toggle for a single yes/no/indeterminate choice.
descriptions.Radio: One option in a mutually-exclusive set, always used inside a RadioGroup.
descriptions.RadioGroup: Coordinates a set of Radio buttons so only one can be selected at a time.
descriptions.Switch: An on/off toggle styled like a physical switch, for immediate-effect settings.
descriptions.Slider: Drag a handle (or two, for a range) along a track to pick a numeric value.
descriptions.Knob: A rotary control for picking a numeric value within a fixed arc.
descriptions.Field: Wraps a form control with a label, help text, and error message, wired together for you.
descriptions.DatePicker: A text field paired with a calendar popover for picking a date or range.
descriptions.Calendar: A month grid for picking a single date, multiple dates, or a range.
descriptions.FileUpload: A drop zone and file list for picking files, with validation and progress.
descriptions.Select: A dropdown for picking one or more values from a list, with search and virtualization.
descriptions.Combobox: A searchable dropdown that also accepts free text, so autocomplete and tagging are one component.
descriptions.CascadeSelect: A dropdown for picking a path through nested options, one level at a time.
descriptions.Tree: A collapsible, indented list for hierarchical data with single or multi-selection.
descriptions.TreeSelect: A dropdown whose panel is a Tree, for picking one or more nodes from a hierarchy.
descriptions.Dialog: A modal overlay that interrupts the page until the user responds or dismisses it.
descriptions.Drawer: A panel that slides in from a viewport edge, for navigation or side content.
descriptions.Popover: A floating panel anchored to a trigger element, for menus, forms, or extra detail.
descriptions.Tooltip: A small floating label that appears on hover or focus to explain an element.
descriptions.BottomSheet: A panel that slides up from the bottom edge, common on touch layouts.
descriptions.ContextMenu: A menu that opens at the pointer on right-click, replacing the native browser menu.
descriptions.Menu: A dropdown list of actions opened from a trigger, with full keyboard navigation.
descriptions.MenuList: The same row rendering as Menu, but always in-flow, built for a permanent sidebar nav.
descriptions.Tabs: Switches between panels of content, with a sliding indicator under the active tab.
descriptions.Toaster: Renders the notifications created by toast(). Mount it once, anywhere in your app.
descriptions.Message: An inline banner for status text: info, success, warning, or error.
descriptions.Progress: A bar or ring showing completion of a determinate or indeterminate task.
descriptions.Loader: A small spinner for indicating that something is in progress.
descriptions.Skeleton: A placeholder shape that mimics real content while it is still loading.
descriptions.DataTable: A data grid with sorting, selection, resizing, and virtualization, composed from Columns.
descriptions.Column: Defines one column of a DataTable, always used inside its tree.
descriptions.Pagination: Page-number controls for splitting a long list or table across pages.
descriptions.Card: A bordered container for grouping related content, with optional title and actions.
descriptions.Avatar: A circular (or square) image or initials, representing a person or entity.
descriptions.Badge: A small dot, count, or label overlaid on the corner of another element.
descriptions.Tag: A compact label for categorizing or annotating an item inline.
descriptions.Chip: A removable, compact token for selected filters, tags, or multi-select values.
descriptions.Kbd: Styles a keyboard shortcut so it reads like a physical key.
descriptions.Accordion: A stack of collapsible sections where opening one can close the others.
descriptions.AccordionItem: One collapsible section of an Accordion, always used inside its tree.
descriptions.Collapsible: A single show/hide section for content that is optional or secondary.
descriptions.Separator: A thin line (or gap) for dividing content into visually distinct groups.
descriptions.Resizable: A draggable handle for letting the user resize a panel between a min and max size.
descriptions.SwipeToReveal: Swipe an item to reveal actions underneath it, like a native mobile list row.
descriptions.PullToRefresh: A pull-down gesture at the top of a scroll container that triggers a refresh.
descriptions.Dock: A macOS-style row of icons that magnify as the pointer approaches them.
